intro: If you're looking for a place to spend the night before shopping Rong Kluea Market, or before crossing the Khlong Luek border into Poipet — My Room by Sermsub is a tiny boutique hotel of just 18 rooms in Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo Province, that review after review agrees is "cleaner and smarter than the price." · The design is an understated, warm-toned minimalist style that feels more like a hotel in a big city than a place by the border · There's a fitness room, massage service, a garden, and 24-hour room service and front desk, plus free Wi-Fi, free parking, and a free shuttle within a short surrounding radius · Rooms start at about ฿800/night · scores around 7.9 from real reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: My Room by Sermsub overview — who it's for — If we put it as briefly as possible, My Room by Sermsub is a small minimalist boutique hotel that suits "people passing through" more than it suits a long, settle-in trip · It isn't a resort that'll have you lounging by a pool all day, and it isn't a big hotel with meeting rooms and a lavish buffet · It's a small place of just 18 rooms in Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo Province, that positions itself as a "clean, quiet room at an easy price" for people who've come for a specific reason · The groups it fits best are shoppers heading to Rong Kluea Market, people who need to cross the Khlong Luek border into Poipet on the Cambodian side, businesspeople with work near the border, and travelers who step off the train or coach at Aranyaprathet and just need somewhere to sleep for one night before moving on · Real reviews echo the same thing: the people most impressed are the ones who "didn't expect a small hotel near the border to be this clean and this nicely done" · It's also certified to the SHA Extra Plus hygiene-safety standard, which adds peace of mind for travelers who care about cleanliness · Put simply, if you set your expectations right — a clean, quiet, smart room, a workable location, an easy price — this place tends to satisfy beyond the number of stars it carries.

Location and getting around — The hotel sits at 168 Moo 2, Thanawithi Road, Ban Mai Nong Sai, Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo Province, a location that lines up neatly with the main reason people come to this town · The two spots most people come to Aranyaprathet for are Rong Kluea Market, one of Thailand's largest wholesale markets for second-hand goods and border merchandise, and Khlong Luek, the border crossing into Poipet, Cambodia — and both are a short drive of about 5–10 minutes from the hotel · On top of that, the hotel itself is about a 10-minute walk to Aranyaprathet train station and roughly a 10-minute drive from the bus terminal, so people arriving on the Bangkok–Aranyaprathet rail line or by coach can settle in without a long onward ride · Around the hotel you'll also find convenience stores, made-to-order eateries, and a big store like Big C close by · A real help for people without a car is the free shuttle within a short surrounding radius (generally about 5 kilometers), which covers Rong Kluea Market, Khlong Luek, and the bus terminal — ask about it and arrange a time with the front desk in advance · One honest note: the lane the hotel sits on is fairly quiet and not on a busy main road lined with shops, so if you want to walk out for a late-night bite it may not be that convenient, and you'll want to lean on the hotel shuttle or call a ride instead.

"I didn't think a hotel near the border would be this clean and this nicely decorated. The room was quiet, the AC nice and cold, slept really well. In the morning they even drove me to Rong Kluea Market for free. Great value for this price."

Room types and decor — My Room by Sermsub has around 18 rooms total, split into several types to choose from by group size and budget · It starts with the Comfort Twin / Comfort Double, compact entry rooms that are well laid out and suit solo travelers or couples focused on one night's sleep · Stepping up are the Superior King / Superior Twin, which are larger and give you more breathing room, and a higher-tier room like the Deluxe King for those who want a bit more comfort · What sets this place apart from guesthouses at a similar price is the warm-toned minimalist design that plays with earth-tone walls, woodwork, and soft lighting for an understated, smart feel like a city boutique hotel, rather than the plain square rooms typical of an upcountry hotel · Every room has air conditioning, a TV, a safe, a minibar, and an en-suite bathroom with a water heater, a shower, a hair dryer, and towels · Many reviews agree that the rooms are very clean, the beds comfortable, and the AC properly cold — the three things overnight travelers care about most · A few reviews note that some decor touches, like the curtains or certain furnishings, are starting to look worn with use, but they also grant that overall it still holds up well and doesn't affect the stay · For people coming to work, the in-room Wi-Fi is stable enough for general use and short online meetings.

On-site facilities and services — Small as it is, My Room by Sermsub still offers facilities that count as more than you'd expect for a hotel at this price near the border · There's a small fitness room for those who want a light workout, and a massage service that's perfect after a full day walking Rong Kluea Market has left your legs aching (ask the front desk about the rate and hours) · There's a small garden to sit and relax in, and common areas decorated in the same tones as the rooms · On the service side, the points that draw praise often are the 24-hour front desk, 24-hour room service, and 24-hour security, which matter a lot for people arriving late or setting off again before dawn · There's daily housekeeping, free parking, free Wi-Fi in every room, and a water dispenser and basic supplies in the common areas · What you should know is that the hotel has no in-house restaurant or large dining room and doesn't focus on a buffet breakfast, so if you expect a full breakfast at the hotel, that isn't its strength — but with made-to-order eateries and convenience stores nearby plus the free shuttle, heading out for food is no trouble.

Food and eating around the area — Let's be straight: the appeal of My Room by Sermsub isn't food at the hotel, because there's no large dining room or breakfast buffet like a resort hotel · So the charm of staying here lies in heading out for good food around Aranyaprathet instead · Within a short drive there are plenty of made-to-order eateries, noodle shops, coffee shops, and roadside spots — especially around Rong Kluea Market and the town center, where there's local fare and Thai–Cambodian border food to try · Many people who come to walk Rong Kluea Market just find their food in the market itself, since it has savory dishes, sweets, and cheap fruit · For breakfast, if you're not in a rush to leave, stop by a coffee shop or a congee–rice-soup place in town; for those heading out before dawn to cross the border or catch the train, pack some food with you or ask the front desk about places that open early · The upside of the hotel not tying you to its food is that you don't pay for a breakfast you might not eat, and you have more freedom to eat as you please — which fits the "use the hotel as a place to sleep, then head out and explore" style that suits a transit town like Aranyaprathet.

Service and guest care — For a small hotel, service is often what decides whether you come away impressed, and My Room by Sermsub does well here · Real reviews speak of friendly, helpful staff — quick check-in and check-out, information on crossing the border, train timetables, and arranging the shuttle to Rong Kluea Market or Khlong Luek · The front desk being open 24 hours means guests arriving late or leaving before dawn don't have to worry about picking up a key or checking out · The free shuttle within a short radius gets mentioned often as genuinely saving both time and travel cost, especially for those who didn't drive themselves · To be fair, since it's a small team, during busy stretches or when staff are few the response can sometimes be slower than usual, and extras like massage or the shuttle are best booked in advance to be sure · Overall, service is a strength that helps keep this place's combined score at a satisfying level.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — Pulling from Trip.com, Agoda, and other booking channels, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the thing mentioned most is the cleanliness of the rooms, which many say exceeds expectations for a hotel near the border, followed by the minimalist decor that looks smart and modern, the nicely cold AC, comfortable beds, friendly staff, and the location that's convenient for Rong Kluea Market, crossing the border, and the train station, with the free shuttle helping a lot · On the gripes side: a common one is that the hotel has no in-house restaurant and doesn't focus on breakfast, so you have to head out for food; the lane it sits on is fairly quiet, making a late-night walk for food inconvenient and leaving you reliant on a ride; some decor and in-room furnishings, like the curtains, are starting to look worn with use; and with only 18 rooms, when Rong Kluea Market is busy or over festivals the rooms can fill up fast, so book ahead · The number of reviews on international platforms is still not large (around 20-something on Trip.com), which is normal for a small place in a secondary town, so read reviews from several sources and check the dates of the latest ones for accuracy · Overall, most of the gripes are manageable by setting expectations right and planning food and transport ahead.

"Very clean room, cute minimalist design, and the staff helped sort out a ride across the border. The only downside is there's no restaurant in the hotel, so at night you have to head out for food. Next time I'll bring some food along."

Price comparison and value — The starting room price at My Room by Sermsub is about ฿800/night for a Comfort room at normal rates, rising to roughly ฿1,000–1,400 in the Superior and Deluxe rooms, or when Rong Kluea Market is busy and over long weekends · Compared with places in the same bracket in Aranyaprathet — say a cheap guesthouse where you might get a plain, design-free room, or a boutique hotel with a pool but a higher price like La Villa Boutique (from about ฿1,200) — My Room by Sermsub sits nicely in the middle: you get a cleaner, better-decorated room than the price suggests, without paying as much as a boutique with a pool · What makes it even better value is the free shuttle within a short radius, which saves on the tuk-tuk or hired-ride cost to Rong Kluea Market and the border on each run · If your main goal is to shop the market, cross the border, or pass through for one night, every baht you spend here buys a room better than its star rating · But if you're after a place with a swimming pool or a full breakfast, at this price you'll need to look at other options built for that specifically.

What to know before you book — A few things help make a stay at My Room by Sermsub smoother · One, arrange the free shuttle in advance — it covers a short radius (about 5 km), reaching Rong Kluea Market, Khlong Luek, and the bus terminal, but tell the front desk your time ahead so they can have a vehicle ready · Two, plan ahead for food — the hotel has no in-house restaurant and doesn't focus on breakfast, so if you arrive late or leave before dawn, buy food to bring along or ask the front desk about places that are open · Three, book ahead when the market is busy — there are only 18 rooms, and over festivals, long weekends, or when traders come to drop off goods at Rong Kluea in numbers, the rooms fill fast · Four, if you're crossing to Poipet, ask the front desk about the border's opening and closing times, the documents, and how to continue on the Cambodian side ahead of time, since the team knows the area and gives good information · Five, compare prices across several platforms and choose a free-cancellation rate first if your travel plans aren't firm, since room prices at small places tend to shift with the time of year and demand.

The verdict — From all the real reviews, My Room by Sermsub is the hotel best suited to people who want a clean, quiet, smartly decorated room at an easy price for a night before walking Rong Kluea Market, crossing the Khlong Luek border, or passing through Aranyaprathet · Its strengths are room cleanliness beyond the price, minimalist design that looks better than places at the same level, cold AC, comfortable beds, helpful staff, and a free shuttle that saves both time and money for those without a car · The parts to brace for are the lack of an in-house restaurant and a location on a fairly quiet lane, which means planning food and transport ahead · If you're after a resort with a swimming pool or a full breakfast, this may not be the answer, and you should consider a boutique with a pool like La Villa Boutique or a larger hotel in town instead · But for the goal that matches its style — a good room, an easy price, a workable location — My Room by Sermsub is a worthwhile pick that does its job better than expected in the border district of Aranyaprathet.

faq.q: Where is My Room by Sermsub · is it near Rong Kluea Market?
faq.a: It's at 168 Moo 2, Thanawithi Road, Ban Mai Nong Sai, Aranyaprathet District, Sa Kaeo Province · about a 5–10 minute drive from Rong Kluea Market and the Khlong Luek crossing (the route to Poipet), and about a 10-minute walk to Aranyaprathet train station · there's a free shuttle within a short surrounding radius — ask and arrange a time with the front desk

faq.q: What's the starting price · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿800/night for a Comfort room · there are Superior Twin/King rooms at around ฿950–1,050 and a higher-tier Deluxe King at around ฿1,300 · prices depend on the time of year and how busy Rong Kluea Market is, so compare across platforms and book ahead since there are only 18 rooms

faq.q: Does the hotel have breakfast or an in-house restaurant?
faq.a: There's no in-house dining room or large restaurant and no focus on a buffet breakfast · but within a short drive there are made-to-order eateries, coffee shops, and convenience stores, especially around Rong Kluea Market and the town center · if you arrive late or leave before dawn, it's a good idea to bring some food along

faq.q: What shuttle service and facilities are there?
faq.a: There's a free shuttle within a short surrounding radius (about 5 km) covering Rong Kluea Market, Khlong Luek, and the bus terminal · plus a fitness room, massage service, a garden, 24-hour room service and front desk, 24-hour security, free Wi-Fi in every room, and free parking · the massage and shuttle are best arranged with the front desk in advance

faq.q: What are the rooms like · are they clean?
faq.a: Rooms are done in a warm-toned minimalist style, clean, with cold AC and comfortable beds, featuring AC, a TV, a safe, a minibar, and an en-suite bathroom with a water heater and hair dryer · many reviews say they're cleaner and smarter than the price for a place near the border · a few reviews say some furnishings are starting to look worn with use

It suits people staying a night before walking Rong Kluea Market, crossing the Khlong Luek border, or passing through Aranyaprathet who value a clean, quiet room at an easy price over full facilities · if you're after a resort with a swimming pool or a full breakfast, a boutique with a pool like La Villa Boutique or a larger hotel in town may be a better fit
